Compute all neutrality statistics from a WithinHostSFS

Source: R/sfs.R
neutralityFromSFS.Rd

Computes Tajima's D, Fu's Fs, and Fay and Wu's H from a single WithinHostSFS object. This is the recommended interface for neutrality testing: build the SFS once, then derive all statistics from it.

Usage

neutralityFromSFS(sfs, n = NULL)

Arguments

sfs

A WithinHostSFS object.

n

Integer. Effective sample size for neutrality tests. For deep sequencing data, do not use raw depth. Default: min(100, meanDepth), where the spectrum's meanDepth slot holds the median depth across sites, as recommended in the tajimaD documentation.

Value

A named list with components:

S

Number of segregating sites.

n

Effective sample size used.

pi

Nucleotide diversity per site, Fay and Wu's \(\hat{\pi}\) on the classes \(i\); this is the value passed to tajimaD and, times the genome length, to fusFs.

theta_W

Watterson's theta per site.

theta_H

Fay and Wu's theta_H per site.

tajimaD

Tajima's D.

fusFs

Fu's Fs, with the number of haplotypes set to \(S + 1\), the infinite-sites maximum. As fusFs explains, it then carries no haplotype information, depends only on \(S\), \(n\) and \(\hat{\pi}\), and is pushed below 0 under neutrality, increasingly so as \(\theta\) grows, so a negative value is not evidence of expansion.

fayWuH

Fay and Wu's H.

sfs_corrected

Whether the input SFS was bias-corrected.

polarization

The input's polarisation, "reference" or "outgroup": which allele theta_H and fayWuH treat as ancestral.

Details

Fay and Wu's H measures an excess of high-frequency derived variants, which can indicate positive selection or genetic hitchhiking (Fay and Wu 2000). It needs the frequency of the derived allele at each site, so the function stops on a folded spectrum (polarization = "none"): folding maps a derived allele at 0.9 and one at 0.1 to the same bin. For Tajima's D and Fu's Fs alone, which need no polarisation, use calcNeutralityTests. An unfolded spectrum built by buildSFS has polarization = "reference": its frequencies are those of the alternative allele, so H here assumes that the reference allele is ancestral at every site, which holds only as far as the reference is close to the population the host was infected from. H is defined as: $$H = \hat{\pi} - \hat{\theta}_H$$ where \(\hat{\pi} = \frac{2}{n(n-1)} \sum_i i (n - i) \xi_i\) and \(\hat{\theta}_H = \frac{2}{n(n-1)} \sum_i i^2 \xi_i\) are Fay and Wu's estimators on the same classes, and \(\xi_i\) is the count of sites with \(i\) derived alleles. Each bin stands for the class \(i\) nearest its midpoint, round(mid * n), held within 1 to \(n - 1\). On matching classes both estimators have the same expectation under neutrality, so H is centred on 0 when every class from 1 to \(n - 1\) is observed and each bin holds one class; the detection threshold, which removes the lowest classes, and wider bins move it (with the default threshold of 0.03 and \(n = 100\), leaving out classes 1 and 2 shifts it by about \(-0.04\theta\)), and \(\hat{\pi}\) carries the \(n/(n-1)\) correction that calcNeutralityTests applies. A negative H indicates an excess of high-frequency variants.

Because H weights the high-frequency classes most, it is uninterpretable when QC has removed them. The function therefore stops on a spectrum whose maxFreq slot is below 1, as it is after flagISNV with the default ISNVFilter, which drops every call above 0.5: H could not then reveal an excess of high-frequency variants, whatever the data. Flag the unfiltered object, before any filter with a lower maxFreq, with ISNVFilter(maxFreq = 1), then buildSFS(fold = FALSE).

The per-site values need the spectrum's genome length, which buildSFS takes from the object; a spectrum without one is an error rather than a set of per-genome values labelled per site.

References

Fay JC, Wu CI (2000). Hitchhiking under positive Darwinian selection. Genetics 155:1405-1413.

Examples

vcf <- system.file("extdata", "test_donor.vcf",
    package = "WithinHostExperiment")
whe <- readWithinHost(vcf,
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(sample_id = "donor"),
    caller = "ivar")
sfs <- buildSFS(whe, genomeLength = 1000L, fold = FALSE)
neutralityFromSFS(sfs)
#> $S
#> [1] 15
#> 
#> $n
#> [1] 100
#> 
#> $pi
#> [1] 0.004580202
#> 
#> $theta_W
#> [1] 0.00289722
#> 
#> $theta_H
#> [1] 0.001924848
#> 
#> $tajimaD
#> [1] 1.60772
#> 
#> $fusFs
#> [1] -0.3911511
#> 
#> $fayWuH
#> [1] 0.002655354
#> 
#> $sfs_corrected
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $polarization
#> [1] "reference"
#>
